proposals.before: Emperor Gaozu appointed Zhan to Wu Commandery, but Zhan petitioned again on his own behalf and was instead made administrator of Yuzhang.
proposals.after: Emperor Gaozu appointed Zhan to Wuxing Commandery, but Zhan petitioned again on his own behalf and was instead made administrator of Yuzhang.
proposals.reason: 吳興郡 is Wuxing Commandery, not Wu Commandery.

proposals.before: He memorialized to impeach the minister of works Xu Xianzhi: "I have heard that serving superiors by upholding the law is respect, and governing subordinates with authority is order.
proposals.after: He memorialized to impeach the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xianzhi: "I have heard that serving superiors by upholding the law is respect, and governing subordinates with authority is order.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works (司空).

proposals.after: He memorialized to impeach the Director of the Imperial Secretariat Xu Xianzhi, saying, "Your servant has heard that serving superiors with observance of statutes is respect, and facing subordinates with awe and dignity is order.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works (司空).

decisions.reason: Chinese 吳興郡 is Wuxing Commandery; rendering it as Wu Commandery (吳郡) drops 興 and names the wrong place. The proposed replacement restores the correct commandery name without other changes.
Same place-name error as the idiomatic: 吳興郡 must be Wuxing Commandery, not Wu Commandery; the repair corrects only that mistranslation.
出為吳興太守 names Wuxing, not Wu Commandery; 'Wu Commandery' omits 興 and confuses distinct commanderies. The replacement is accurate.
Literal likewise misreads 吳興太守 as Wu Commandery; Wuxing Commandery matches the Chinese, and the rest of the sentence is unchanged and correct.
奏劾尚書令徐羨之 titles Xu as 尚書令 (Director of the Imperial Secretariat), not 司空 (Minister of Works). The repair corrects that office title only.
Same office mistranslation in the literal: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works; the proposed wording is accurate and complete.
